facts.raw_span: A 55-year-old man underwent right hemicolectomy for moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
staged as IIIB (T4N1M0)
He had no thrombophilic disorders
Preoperative carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and CA19-9 levels were normal
He completed six months of adjuvant chemotherapy
Thirteen months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
hepatitis B and C serologies were negative
Tumor markers including CEA, CA19-9, α-fetoprotein, and PIVKA-II were all within normal limits
CTA demonstrated a liver tumor with two components: a solid portion that enhanced in the early phase and washed out in the delayed phase, and a cystic component
CTAP showed absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect throughout the right lobe, suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus
Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography showed no communication with the biliary tree
bile cytology was negative for malignancy

CTAP shows absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect, suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus.
The patient has a liver lesion, which is consistent with a liver tumor.
The patient has a history of adenocarcinoma of the colon, which is the primary cancer.

rationales.F01: Patient has a history of colon cancer, which increases the likelihood of colorectal cancer liver metastasis.
rationales.F06: A liver lesion was found on follow-up CT, which could be a metastasis from the primary colon cancer.
rationales.F09: The liver tumor has characteristics consistent with a metastasis, such as early enhancement and delayed washout.
rationales.F10: The absence of the right portal vein and perfusion defect suggest portal vein tumor thrombus, which is often associated with liver metastasis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon and the presence of a liver tumor with characteristics suggestive of metastasis, along with the absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect, support this diagnosis.
